shell.test.ts pins the exact sorted TUI tool list: it names review_confirm_plan and review_decide_premise (lines 880-881) but not review_complete, which completeSpec now registers (operator-confirm-review.ts:792). The test was not updated by the PR. No signal that the omission is deliberate.

In review_complete.apply (operator-confirm-review.ts:750-775), completeReviewGated closes the round before the press record is written. A failed write falls into the catch that says 'nothing was recorded', yet the review is closed, and buildCard then refuses it as already complete (line 716). Writing the record after success matches AC4 ('a refused gate records nothing'), but nothing indicates that the post-close failure window and the false message were chosen. No comment gives a reason for the ordering.

AC4 (acceptance-criteria.md:19) says the card shows the reviewed head 'taken from the package, not from model input'. The card accepts a model-supplied head (operator-confirm-review.ts:703, 711) and shows it as the reviewed head (line 725), with the recorded head not shown beside it. The CLI --head flag (managed.ts ~969) is an operator-typed input and warns when it replaces the recorded head; a model-supplied one on an operator card contradicts the AC. The '(given by the agent...)' label is introduced by this PR and cannot ratify it. A review-security-code finding can only be upheld or challenged, and no signal justifies challenging it.

The reviewer concedes the CLI behaviour is pre-existing. The base text of SKILL.detail.md:669 already told the agent 'then you run `keryx review complete`', and the base cli-reference already said the agent runs `keryx review complete` after the waiver cards. AC5 requires the terminal commands to keep working 'exactly as before', and AC7 forbids only sending the operator to a terminal, not the agent running the command. The PR's added clause 'or run `keryx review complete`' therefore keeps an accepted prior path. Against that, the PR now lists `complete` as an operator-only step needing a terminal (cli-reference.md:4921) and AC9 treats 'complete' as an operator act. Whether the final yes must be the only agent path to complete is a product choice the code cannot settle. This is a security finding, so it is held rather than downgraded or dismissed.
premises.question: The card is meant to give the operator a final yes on closing a review, but the review-orchestrator SKILL.detail.md still tells the agent it may instead run the pre-existing `keryx review complete`, which closes the round without that yes. Keep the 'or run' path as before, or make the card the only agent path?
options: dismiss — keep 'or run keryx review complete' as the pre-existing agent path (the card is an additional option)
uphold — drop the 'or run' clause, make the card the only agent path to complete, and align cli-reference, TM-04 and autonomous-review

AC5 and AC6 hold only on the pre-flight unmirrored path (lines 6101-6107). No signal of intent.

operator-confirm-review-tools.test.ts:630-641 asserts only `toContain('nothing was recorded')` for a stamped report with no evidence level. Any thrown error in apply produces that same string, so the test does not show which gate refused. The head, waiver, run-profile and routing refusals are never driven through the card. AC4 asks for 'a refused gate' (singular), but the weak assertion is still a real gap in a sensitive criterion, and the gates' own unit tests do not exercise the card's apply path.

A sixth positional parameter on answerChunkEstimate and a fifth on recordCoverageWaiver does cross the usual argument-count guidance. The base signatures already had trailing optional positionals (`now`, `confirmedVia`; chunks-estimate.ts:160, coverage-complete.ts:213 at base), so the PR extends an existing shape. That shows accretion, not a recorded reason, and the project has no rule on options objects (.metaproject/rules searched). Neighbouring recorders added in the same area (answerPremiseQuestion, recordPlanConfirmation, recordOperatorDecision) take an input object. No cited intent signal or practice source supports a challenge.

The card lists manifest readiness_waivers plus the research coverage waiver (operator-confirm-review.ts:668-675) and omits mutation-waiver and reviewer-override decisions from operator-decisions.json. The completion gates read only premise decisions (verdict.ts:10, readiness.ts:20 import only the premise type), so nothing here is a bypass, as the reviewer says. AC4 says 'every waiver with its item and operator quote', and 'item' matches the readiness and coverage waivers. The card's own description says 'every waiver the package carries', and a mutation waiver does lower the evidence behind the close. Whether a mutation waiver counts as a waiver for this card is a product choice that AC4 does not settle.
premises.question: The review_complete card shows readiness and coverage waivers but not the mutation waivers recorded in operator-decisions.json. Should the card list them too?
options: uphold — add mutation waivers (and reviewer overrides) to the card
dismiss — the card shows only the waivers the completion gates act on (readiness and coverage); the evidence level line already covers the mutation pass

premises.reasoning: The invariant 'pressedBy/pressedAt only with remote-card' is documented on CardPress (types.ts:92) and enforced only in operatorConfirmTool.invoke (operator-confirm-tools.ts:207-227). cardPressFields and the recorders spread whatever press they receive next to any confirmedVia. The only caller that supplies a press today is correct, so this is defence-in-depth on an audit field, not an active bug. There is no intent signal for leaving it unenforced.

review/estimate.ts:199-200 redeclares pressedBy/pressedAt although CardPress is available in the same review domain and is used by sibling modules (coverage-complete.ts:32, chunks-estimate.ts). Other domains (flow, learning, harness) may reasonably avoid importing review/types, but the in-domain duplicate is a plain DRY miss. No signal of intent.

tui-shell.ts:6103-6105 and 6116-6131 call operatorCards.ask before an awaited inner/raceApproval and answer after it, with no try/finally. A rejected dock leaves an unanswered entry, and OperatorConfirmationLog never evicts unanswered entries (operator-confirmations.ts:53-56). Pairing a registration with a finally is accepted practice, and no signal shows rejection was ruled out.

AC6 asks for the time left of the 1-hour token on each pending remote confirmation, which explains the countdown. But pendingConfirmationLine (operator-confirmations.ts:102-108) also prints a token countdown, or 'token expired, ask again', for an unmirrored card, which has no token, and for a card the shell can still answer. waiting() ignores expiry (lines 61-63). This is a display defect inside what the AC allows.

answer() evicts the earliest-asked answered entries (operator-confirmations.ts:53-56) and entries() reverses ask order (line 68), while its comment says 'newest first' for answered cards. A card asked early and answered late is evicted before one asked later and answered sooner. No signal of intent.

autonomous-review.md:35 (added by this PR) says an autonomous run 'stops at the floor'. The same doc defines the floor status as exit 3 for an action that always needs a human (lines 28, 44-49). The same PR's unattended.ts:57-60 says the run 'records the item as Not run', and the review-orchestrator SKILL says 'unattended, the item is Not run'. The doc contradicts the PR's own code comment.

operator-confirm-tools.ts:206 deletes the pending token before the allowed-id (215) and TTL (218) checks, so every refusal spends the token. CHANGELOG.md:18 says such an answer 'changes nothing'. That is true of the records, but a reader would expect a retry on the same card to work. TM-04 line 104 says 'Each refusal leaves the token spent', but that line comes from this PR and cannot ratify the CHANGELOG wording. One sub-claim looks wrong: the 15-minute wait. The shell passes MAX_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 minutes (remote/protocol.ts:169; tui-shell.ts:6122). The finding still stands on the changelog wording and the 'carries this question's token' phrasing.

TM-04 section 6a (lines 106-112) says a press proves 'pressed yes on this card'. Line 111 covers the bot token being reachable by the agent and line 112 says the answer does not prove the operator saw the card text last shown, but neither says that a bot-token holder can edit the mirrored card's text. A press then proves a press on a card with the real approval id, not that the operator read the text the shell holds. AC7's three limits are present, but the 'this card' claim overstates; the new wording is introduced by this PR and cannot ratify itself. A review-security-code finding can only be upheld or challenged, and nothing justifies a challenge.
